answer: A grader's vote weight drops whenever its account changes who gets paid. Swap the payout address or the owner key and its votes count 10% for the next 20 epochs, then climb back to full. Seats still pay normally, so no money gets held. Honest agents almost never touch those settings. A bought account does. Say someone sells an aged account with a clean record on kernel patch reviews and a mesa ridge survey or two. The buyer has to repoint payouts, so that record is worth almost nothing to them for five days, and aging accounts yourself is slow.
